name: vol_views
description: Ask the installed Volatility 3 one named question about an image and keep its whole answer: offline, as the engine printed it, with its scope and a status. `question` names a plugin as the installed `vol --offline --help` lists it (a module name such as windows.pslist is enough when one class is listed under it); a name that is not listed is refused as JSON, naming it, and a module with several classes is refused, naming them: no plugin runs that the listing does not show. It serves the questions the kickoff recipe (memory-windows) does not ask, Linux and macOS images once a symbol table has been validated, and reruns; it interprets nothing the plugin prints. `readiness` is required: the answer of vol_readiness for this image (views plugins and symbols), passed as a file under the run directory (a declared job input); its verdict must be ready and its inputs.path must be this image. The receipt is read, not verified: the tool lists the plugins itself and runs offline whatever the receipt says. `pid` (a list of integers) is passed as the plugin's --pid and `dump` as the plugin's own dump option (--dump, or --dump-regions); each only when the plugin's --help lists it, otherwise the call is refused before the plugin runs. WHAT IS KEPT: every line the engine prints is split at its tabs (the quick renderer's column separator) and each cell is judged by the shared SHOWN rules (a part that looks like a secret is replaced; withholding is by shape, so a plain password or a name under 16 characters is printed); the lines are paged: `limit` lines (default 100, at most 1000) in the answer and the whole judged output, one JSON object per line, in a file under tool-output (in a job $OUT/tool-output) that `output.all_results` names, with its size and sha256 (`output.file_bytes`, `output.file_sha256`) when there are more lines than `limit`; with fewer, the answer holds them all. The raw output, as the engine wrote it, is memory content (command lines, environments, process names): it is written only with `write_values` (default false) in a job run as secret output, to $OUT/vol_views/vol_views-<digest>-output.txt (directory mode 0700, file mode 0600, created exclusively under a hidden name and placed without replacing an earlier file), and so are the files the plugin exports with `dump` (under $OUT/vol_views/artefacts-<digest>, passed to Volatility as -o); the sizes and sha256 of the raw output and of each exported file are in $OUT/vol_views/manifest.jsonl, never in the answer, and secret_values names what was written. `dump` without write_values is refused. This manifest declares secret_output for write_values, so the harness seals such a job as sensitive, and the tool checks SECRET_OUTPUT=1 and refuses as JSON, before it looks at the image, when write_values is set outside a job or in a job that is not secret output. The status is complete when the plugin ran to its end with exit 0 and its whole output was read, judged and kept; it is partial when the plugin was ended (its time, or more than 1 GiB of output, or 64 MiB of log read), when the engine's log says pages were missing (a heuristic over the log's wording, not a proof), when a line longer than 1 MiB was not judged, when the plugin printed no row, or when the clock ended a digest or a listing; failed when the plugin exits non-zero. A complete status is not a claim about the image: the plugin's scope is its own, and an empty or short output is an absence only after the plugin completed with the matching symbol table. OFFLINE: every Volatility call carries `--offline`; the tool fetches nothing; a caller's text reaches Volatility only as an image path (made absolute), a symbol directory and a number for --pid; the plugin runs from the directory /, so nothing it writes by default lands in the run directory. THE CLOCK: `max_seconds` (default 420, at most 540, inside timeout_seconds 600); each program gets what is left less a 10 s reserve and, past its own time (help 90 s, the plugin's --help 60 s) or output cap, is ended with what it started, in this tool's own process group (never a session of its own, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on Linux); SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it and answer once with status failed, interrupted true, the files being written kept under a name ending in .partial, exit 128 plus the signal; a signal that arrives while the answer is written is held until it is out. Not measured: the real Volatility was not available where this tool was written. The listing (one dotted plugin name per line under the Plugins section), the options -q, -o, -s, -f and --offline and exit status 1 for a failure were read from the Volatility 3 2.28.2 source; the plugin's own --pid and dump options are looked up in its --help; the lines judged are the quick renderer's tab-separated table, which the tests' stand-in imitates, not a recorded run. symbols_dir may not contain a semicolon (-s reads a semicolon-separated list). A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 2: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

path.description: The memory image the question is asked about. It is opened without waiting and looked at with fstat first: a FIFO, a directory or an empty file is refused.

question.description: The plugin to run, as the installed vol lists it (windows.pslist, linux.lsof.Lsof)

readiness.description: A file under the run directory holding the answer of vol_readiness for this image (views plugins and symbols), verdict ready

pid.description: Process ids to ask about (the plugin's --pid), at most 64; only for a plugin that lists --pid

dump.description: Run the plugin's own dump option and keep what it exports. Needs write_values. Default false.

write_values.description: Keep the raw output (and, with dump, the exported files) in the job. Only in a job run as secret output. Default false.

symbols_dir.description: A directory of symbol tables to search besides vol's own (passed as `-s`)

max_seconds.description: The clock of the whole call, 10 to 540 (default 420)

limit.description: How many judged output lines the answer lists inline, 1 to 1000 (default 100); the whole judged output is kept in a file the answer names
